beats.beat: The core business is processing minerals into specialty chemicals: Functional Additives (FA), Chemically Modified Minerals (CMM), Soft Minerals (SM) and Hard Minerals (HM).
The filing lists a diversified product portfolio and diversified user industries as competitive strengths.

How sales happen: a long-term arrangement with corporate promoter 20 Microns Limited to market and sell products through their network; the company calls the support of its holding company a strength.
Sale terms are not contracted: the company has no long-term or definitive agreements with customers and relies on purchase orders for volume, pricing and other terms.
Raw material purchases are on the same footing — no long-term agreements with suppliers, so timely supply and competitive prices are not assured.
Customer concentration: top 10 customers made up about 59% of revenue from operations in FY15, 57% in FY16, and 59% in FY17.
Export footprint: ₹10.68 crore of exports over the past five years to Nigeria, Saudi Arabia and Sri Lanka.

Physical footprint: manufacturing at Plot 347, GIDC Waghodia, Vadodara, and Plot 104/3, Thenkasi Road, Pathur Village, Tirunelveli, Tamil Nadu; administrative offices in Bhuj and Udaipur; the new capex is at Plot 336, GIDC Waghodia.
R&D and product innovation, plus a strong management team, are listed among strengths.

beats.beat: Restated figures are the company's financials as reworked for the offer document to common accounting standards — this is the table an investor should read.
The restated P&L covers six periods: six months to 30 September 2017 and full years FY13 to FY17.
PAT turned from a ₹0.27 crore loss in FY13 and a ₹0.12 crore loss in FY14 to a ₹1.50 crore profit in FY15, then ₹0.90 crore in FY16, ₹1.75 crore in FY17 and ₹1.33 crore in H1 FY18.
Earnings per share followed the same arc: -₹0.45 in FY13, -₹0.20 in FY14, ₹2.47 in FY15, ₹1.46 in FY16, ₹2.43 in FY17, ₹1.48 in H1 FY18.
Operating cash flow is the warning: ₹2.01 crore in FY13, ₹1.28 crore in FY14, ₹4.22 crore in FY15, ₹8.03 crore in FY16, then -₹3.50 crore in FY17, and ₹1.25 crore in H1 FY18.
Total assets stood at ₹34.25 crore as of 30 September 2017, up from ₹30.19 crore at FY13 year-end, with a dip through the middle years.

beats.beat: Control: promoters are 20 Microns Limited (corporate promoter) and individuals Chandresh S. Parikh, Atil C. Parikh and Rajesh C. Parikh.
Pre-issue, promoters hold 89,48,270 equity shares — 99.76% of the paid-up capital. The rest, 21,510 shares or 0.24%, sits with the promoter group.
Authorised capital is ₹2,000 lakh; issued, subscribed and paid-up capital is ₹897 lakh as of 30 September 2017.
Related-party transactions exist for at least the last five years; the DRHP cross-refers to the financial statements for details.

Governance flags: the company does not own premises for some manufacturing facilities and administrative offices; its corporate logo is not registered; there have been past non-filings, incorrect filings or delays with the Registrar of Companies, in some cases resolved with additional fees; and certain statutory approvals for the Plot 9-10, GIDC Waghodia facility had not yet been obtained.
Contingent liabilities were ₹29.11 lakh as of 30 September 2017.
Legal proceedings exist involving the company, promoters, group companies and directors; an adverse decision could have a material effect.

beats.beat: The company sits in India's specialty chemicals market — a segment CRISIL Research put at roughly ₹1,000 billion, about 17% of the Indian chemicals industry, which was estimated at ₹5,800–6,200 billion in fiscal 2017.
Specialty chemicals grew at 10–12% CAGR from fiscal 2014 to 2017; CRISIL forecasts 12–14% CAGR ahead.
The market is highly fragmented, with SMEs holding 70–75% share; only a few Indian players have the scale or capability to compete with global giants on product development and innovation.

Growth drivers named in the filing: increased intensity of consumption, improved consumption standards, end-use demand from a middle class that could reach 148 million households by 2030, and government support including 100% FDI and a Draft National Chemical Policy.

Specific headwinds: India's chemicals industry has imported more than it exported every year from FY13 to FY17, with imports growing at 6.4% CAGR versus 6% for exports; exports to the EU face REACH regulation.
Downstream demand in plastics is strong: CRISIL expects polymer demand to grow at 9–10% CAGR and plastic products at 11–13% CAGR between fiscals 2017 and 2020.

beats.beat: 20 Microns Nano Minerals Limited is a Gujarat-based processor and seller of specialty chemicals — functional additives, chemically modified minerals, plus soft and hard minerals.
Its sales model runs through a long-term arrangement: the corporate promoter, 20 Microns Limited, markets and sells the company's products through its network.
The IPO money is earmarked for a new manufacturing facility at Plot 336, GIDC Waghodia, Vadodara, general corporate purposes, and a listing on NSE's SME platform, NSE EMERGE.
The document is a draft red herring prospectus, so issue size and price can still change; what follows is what the draft discloses.

beats.beat: No long-term contracts: sales run on purchase orders and raw material supply has no long-term agreements, so volume, price and margins can move with every order.
Customer concentration: top ten customers supplied roughly 59% of revenue in each of the last three full years; without long-term contracts, losing one large buyer would hit the top line immediately.
Promoter-led sales: revenue depends on a long-term arrangement under which corporate promoter 20 Microns Limited markets and sells the company's products through its network.
Regulatory gaps: not all statutory approvals for the Plot 9-10, GIDC Waghodia facility have been obtained, and past RoC filings have been late or incorrect, exposing the company to penalties.
Negative cash flow: operating cash flow was -₹3.50 crore in FY17 despite a profit of ₹1.75 crore; the DRHP itself warns sustained negative cash flow could affect growth and business.
